entry.title: TwitchSentry v4.1.0-beta.1: (TESTERS NEEDED) Bot waves, text waves, viewbot alarm and Silent Bot Protection (pre-release)
entry.content:
This is a BETA! PLEASE test it out as much as you can, but do not use it as daily driver! Some translations may be missing, some features can be broken, intentionally not working, have misleading description or crash unexpectedly. Happy to hear about feedback here!

✨ Added

  • Bot wave check: the Spam Filter counts the brand-new chatters whose first message names the same address within a window (60 s and 5 senders by default, more during a raid, scaled with its size). Once enough share one, that address is decisive for everyone still in the window: the messages already posted get the Default Action in one go, with one undo entry for all of them, every further message naming it goes, and the Spam Learner adds the address to the spam domains. Regulars are never touched, Twitch links and the Link Filter's allowed domains never count. On by default (Spam Scoring → Bot Wave: 'Detect Bot Waves'); the shared bot list gets the wave's accounts with the reason bot_wave.

  • Text wave check: catches chat bot tools that post the lines of a list from several bought accounts in turn, without a link. Once three accounts that are not regulars here have posted the same words within 10 minutes, those words are decisive for everyone still in the window, the earlier messages get the Default Action with one undo entry, and the accounts reach the shared bot list as text_wave. Words a regular posted never count, nor do commands, short lines or emote spam, and it rests for ten minutes after a raid. On by default (Spam Scoring → Text Wave: 'Detect Text Waves'). It also catches a single account rotating a list: two different lines, each posted twice or more within the window, from an account that is not a regular here; channel bots like Nightbot never count (Spam Scoring → Text Wave: 'Detect Rotating Accounts', on).

  • Viewbot alarm: Silent Bot Protection compares Twitch's viewer count with the people in chat on every Present Viewers round. When the count jumps (25 viewers and 50 percent within 10 minutes by default), no raid brought them and chat did not grow along, it alerts you, sets a stream marker and writes every count until the spike is over to Logs/viewbot-evidence.txt, for a report to Twitch. It never acts on its own. On by default, with its own switch and a notification switch on every platform (Silent Bot Protection → Viewbot Alarm: 'Viewbot Alarm').

  • Code injection check: the Message Filter can act on messages built to run as code in an overlay, a TTS voice or an action that hands chat on: HTML and script tags, TTS tags, shell and PowerShell commands, Log4Shell lookups, SQL and paths out of a folder or to another computer. Scored like caps and emotes, off by default (Message Filter → Code Injection: 'Code Injection Check Enabled').

  • tsRaid toggles: the deck button takes on, off and toggle like tsHateRaid and tsFollowWave; arm and disarm still work.

  • !permitme: viewers can ask for a link permit in chat. The request waits on the OBS dock's Permit list and for a tsPermit key like a Channel Points request, and a moderator's !permit answers it too. Off by default (Permit → Chat Requests: 'Accept !permitme').

🔧 Changed

  • LurkBot Filter is now Silent Bot Protection: it now covers two kinds of bots that never write, the silent accounts in the viewer list and the viewbots behind a viewer spike. Everything carries the new name: the page, alerts and their switches, the Twitch ban reason, Logs/silentbot-finds.txt (the old file and its monthly copies are renamed), the settings (sb*, useSilentBotProtection, taken over from lb* once), the deck (tsSilentBot, tsModule "Silent Bot Protection"; the old names no longer work). The Shared Bot List keeps its public file lurkbots.json, so older versions keep their bans.

  • ASCII art and Zalgo text hang off the Flood check: both moved into the Flood card and only work while 'Flood Check Enabled' is on (Message Filter → Flood).

  • A moderator's !permit answers a waiting request: a viewer's Channel Points request leaves the Permit list with it, and its points are spent instead of given back later.

  • Test mode, Raid and Follow Wave keys say On: tsTitle = auto no longer shows the time the window ends, which read like a countdown; {until} still gives it.

  • Spam feed v7: the pirate-streaming wave of 2026-10-31 (dovie .tv, eight sentences in rotation from brand-new accounts): the domain and its wordings join the shared lists, so the hidden address and the pitch make two categories and the message goes.

🐛 Fixed

  • Bot wave bar after a raid: the Spam Filter kept scaling its bot wave bar with the last raid Raid Protection had seen, long after the raid window had closed, so after a big raid a wave needed far more senders until the next raid. It now counts a raid only while Raid Protection's window is open or for five minutes after any raid, and Raid Protection clears the size when it disarms.

  • Streamer.bot Deck buttons: [TS] - Deck recognises the deck a button sits on, so a press that went wrong shows a notification on that deck. A button that names its item with tsDeckItemId carries its title and colour, and the import redraws such buttons every 10 seconds. A Deck switch whose sides pass the argument as a Boolean carries its title and colour on both sides and turns itself when the state changes elsewhere.

entry.title: Classic Chat Gamble v25.2.3: The window in French and Brazilian Portuguese
entry.content:
Added

  • French and Brazilian Portuguese. The settings window comes in English, German, Spanish, French and Brazilian Portuguese (the pencil, then Language). In Spanish, French and Portuguese the buttons, the pages and the settings all UIFramework games share are translated; the odds, the game's own messages and How to play stay English. German still covers every setting and message.
  • Blocked groups and Addicted groups suggest your Streamer.bot groups. Click into the field and the groups not added yet show below it; typing narrows the list, Enter or a click adds one.

Changed

  • The settings action is 0.3.2, the host block UIFramework 2.0.0's; the window offers UIFramework 2.0.0 at its next open. Nothing in your settings changes.

Fixed

  • A gamble during a save plays on your settings. For a moment while the window saves, configs.json is being swapped, and a !gamble that came then played on the defaults. It now waits for the saved file, or reads the .bak.
  • A Fairness stop picked just before saving is saved. Its numbers could arrive while the game checked the settings; the window said Saved and the file kept the old ones. Slid across several stops, the slider now keeps the numbers of the stop it ends on.
  • The Log page shows gambles of the same second newest first, and its folder button opens Chat Games\Logs beside Streamer.bot, also after an export to another folder.
  • A UIFramework too new for this game no longer locks the window. The update notice at Streamer.bot's start loaded the newest one installed, also one another game had brought for a newer settings action, and the window then failed at every start. It now loads one that fits. The notice no longer names a version you skipped with No, and a damaged UIFramework.dll is set aside and offered again even while an older one runs.

entry.title: Battleship Game v2.4.2: The update question says when to restart Streamer.bot
entry.content:
Added

  • The settings window in French and Brazilian Portuguese, beside English, German and Spanish. Battleship's own settings are labelled in English and German; the other three show them in English.

Removed

  • The About page's Discord link. It led to Blackjack's post on the Streamer.bot Discord; Battleship has none.

Changed

  • The update question says when Streamer.bot needs a restart. A newer UIFramework can be used at once only while none is running in your Streamer.bot; otherwise it takes effect after a restart. The dialog now says which of the two it is, and after such a download a note says it again: restart when it suits you, everything goes on as before until then.
  • Closing the update question means "not now". Yes takes the new UIFramework, No skips that version, and Cancel, the X and Esc ask again at the next open. Closing the dialog used to skip the version for good.
  • A skipped version is skipped in every game. It is kept once, in UIFramework\loader.json beside Streamer.bot, and so is "autoUpdate": false. What a game's uiframework.layout.json holds is still read.
  • The settings action is 0.3.2, the host block UIFramework 2.0.0's. Nothing in your settings changes; the window offers UIFramework 2.0.0 on its next open.
  • The !bstats and !ballstats replies are on the Messages page, under Stats: Stats reply, Stats reply in Free game and Leaderboard. The default reply is the old one without the flawless wins, best win and current streak, which {flawless}, {bestWin} and {streak} add back.
  • In Free game !ballstats ranks by ships sunk, as no points are won or lost, and !bstats leaves out the net.
  • The overlay is version 18; an older copy is replaced on the next command and kept as a .bak.

Fixed

  • A download GitHub does not deliver, or one that breaks off, is tried three times before the settings action gives up.
  • The game hears of every save. When the game action was busy at that moment, the save passed it by, and the overlay and Click to Fire were not brought up to date. The save is now sent again, three tries in all, and a note beside the window says if it still did not arrive. A command in the moment a save is written reads the saved settings, not the defaults.
  • A save keeps what changed while the game checked it. A preset pressed meanwhile was lost although the window said "Saved"; it now counts as unsaved.
  • The update notice takes an older UIFramework when the newest one is damaged, and no longer names a UIFramework release you skipped with No or while the release check is off.
  • Fire with sample values on the Help page no longer freezes the window while the game is busy, and says why no answer came.
  • The Log page's folder button opens the log folder beside Streamer.bot, also after an export elsewhere, and battles logged in the same second show newest first.
  • No answer from the game shows as no answer. A Try button said "done" and a table showed as empty when the game action did not answer.
  • A late answer is not taken for the next one. Every request to the game has a variable of its own.
  • The settings window opens with a too-new UIFramework installed. As Streamer.bot started, the game loaded the newest UIFramework, also one that needs a newer settings action, and the window then stayed shut until a restart. It now loads the newest one its settings action fits. When another game has such a UIFramework running already, opening the settings says so in one message, asking to update this game, instead of advising to delete that UIFramework's folder.
  • Points go to the right variable with Currency Core or LOYALTY POINTS. Try the demo, Show a sample round and Add to OBS in the settings window, and a chat command arriving just as a battle paid out, could send later refunds and payouts to the box's variable (points). LOYALTY POINTS is now found the way the window finds it.
  • Switching Free game over a damaged settings file keeps your settings. It wrote a file holding nothing but Free game, over the good backup; now the switch goes into the backup and the damaged file is kept as .broken.
  • !fire link cannot take over somebody else's clicks. In the chat's battle and in a duel, the one clicker it linked could be another viewer, even one of the other side, whose clicks then counted for the wrong person in every later battle. A click from a logged-out viewer, whose id changes with every page load, is linked for that battle only, and an old one no longer keeps the first click from taking control.
  • Click to Fire works after a restart before anyone types a command. A channel-point reward or a save that came first handed the overlay an empty action, and every click failed.
  • The overlay no longer sticks on a finished battle. Two writes at once could fail, or an older state land after a newer one and leave the next battle's clicks unanswered.
  • A click uses up a viewer's vote only when it was sent, on a square still open. The countdown ring keeps time after a reload or a scene switch. The Heat file read mid-write no longer drops both connections.
  • A vote cast while the round is being counted is refused, instead of drawn on the overlay and then wiped. A viewer who voted by click and by !fire and then linked keeps one ballot.
  • Two duel commands of one viewer at the same moment no longer create points.
  • After a moderator's stop nothing more is charged, also when a shot was still being resolved.
  • A command in the moment before the boards are dealt no longer throws an error.
  • The automatic leaderboard reset runs before a battle is recorded, not only when somebody types !bstats, which cleared the new period's first battles with the old ones. Switching it on, or between weekly and monthly, clears nothing. Weeks follow ISO 8601, so New Year's Day no longer starts a second week. A reset of everything no longer restarts the daily winnings cap.
  • !ballstats lists a player who broke even, and answers in Free game. !bstats names the points as the game does with Currency Core or LOYALTY POINTS. A Stats message left empty sends nothing.
  • The Admiral keeps track of a damaged ship when ships touch.
  • Add to OBS finds a scene whose name differs only in case, and says so when OBS created nothing.
  • The Log page's Result filter offers what the log holds: NO-SHOW and STARTED, not four values never written.
  • battleCurrency in the custom triggers is empty for the chat's battle and for a battle begun in Free game.
  • The log file's name uses the Gregorian calendar on every system.
  • The import precompiles the game action again, so the update notice, the custom triggers and the overlay's cleanup run as Streamer.bot starts. Each action's comment names the version again.

Download v2.4.2 · Battleship Game on aaskjer.github.io

entry.title: Hangman Game v13.3.2: Fixes for stakes, the word list, the board and the overlay
entry.content:
Added

  • The window in French and Brazilian Portuguese, beside English, German and Spanish: the pencil at the bottom left, then the language. In Spanish, French and Portuguese the window's own texts and the settings all chat games share are translated; Hangman's own settings and messages stay English there. German has them all.

Changed

  • A reward that starts the round leaves !hm to moderators on Twitch. Viewers start a round there with the reward only; moderators and the broadcaster can still use the command, !hm blitz included.
  • The reset day of the board is a day of the month. Twitch: reset on day (and YouTube's, Kick's) clears that board every month on that day, the last day in a shorter month, with or without the monthly switch. It used to work only together with the monthly switch, and a 29, 30 or 31 skipped the months that are shorter.
  • The board is checked for its reset every day the game runs, with the first round, guess or board command, not only with the first board command of a month. The days played before somebody asked for the board are no longer cleared with the old month.
  • A board of more than 10 places comes as a few longer messages, so a top 25 no longer sends 26 chat lines in a row. Ties are ranked by letters found, then by name.
  • Spaces, hyphens and apostrophes don't matter in a word guess, and the letters are all a word hides: digits and signs show from the start, so R2-D2 and Pac-Man can be solved.
  • The OBS overlay shows one round at a time. With rounds on two platforms at once, the one that started first keeps the overlay until it ends. The overlay is version 11 and replaces an older copy on the next round.
  • Imported words get the topic's name in the import's language as their category (Länder, Videospiele, …).
  • The update question says when Streamer.bot needs a restart. A newer UIFramework can be used at once only while none is running in your Streamer.bot; otherwise it takes effect after a restart. The dialog now says which of the two it is, and after such a download a note says it again: restart when it suits you, everything goes on as before until then.
  • Closing the update question means "not now". Yes takes the new UIFramework, No skips that version, and Cancel, the X and Esc ask again at the next open. Closing the dialog used to skip the version for good.
  • A skipped version is skipped in every game. It is kept once, in UIFramework\loader.json beside Streamer.bot, and so is "autoUpdate": false. What a game's uiframework.layout.json holds is still read. The chat notice at Streamer.bot's start no longer names a version you skipped, nor any while the check is off.
  • The settings action is 0.3.2, the host block UIFramework 2.0.0's, and the settings offer UIFramework 2.0.0 the next time they open. Nothing in your settings changes.

Fixed

  • A typed stake can no longer be higher than the reward's cost. A viewer could type any number into a reward with text input and win it back many times over in your currency; such a redemption is now refused and refunded.
  • A broken word list is kept before the defaults replace it, as Hangman-Wordlist.json.<date-time>.broken. A word list another program held open for a moment was replaced by the 15 default words.
  • The monthly reset clears every player, not only the ones with a win. Played rounds, letters, losses and points of everyone else stayed.
  • The board and !hml know every player, not only the ones with a win: a board without winners said "no scoreboard data yet", and a search for someone who never won found nobody. !hml takes the whole name now, with or without the @.
  • Hidden from the board hides those names even while Include the bot is on.
  • Blocked users cannot start a round, by command or by reward (the reward is refunded).
  • Rounds only during ads holds for rewards too; a redemption outside an ad break is refunded.
  • The IGDB client ID and secret are kept after the first import, as the Words page says.
  • An import that takes longer than the window waits writes nothing. It used to write the words after the window had given up on it, where the next save could take them away again. The first OdeNet download goes on in the background instead of holding the import.
  • Words the list holds with umlauts (Österreich) are found again by an import that writes them out (oesterreich).
  • A fixed import difficulty above your highest difficulty is pointed out in the answer.
  • Points are not paid when the balance cannot be read, instead of overwriting it with the reward alone.
  • Free mode from chat no longer empties configs.json when the file is being saved by the window at that moment.
  • Several chat lines at once no longer mix up who guessed. Runs of the game action take turns.
  • A time-up counts as a loss in the player's stats, as it already broke their streak.
  • The hint is not sent with the guess that loses the round, and the check before saving warns when blitz rounds end before their hint.
  • A repeated letter, a wrong word tried again or a guess that is no guess no longer counts toward the rate limit, and the last one no longer makes you a player of the round.
  • The full figure shows only with the last life gone, also with many lives.
  • The time reminder is sent after an Evil Hangman glitch that covered its second, instead of not at all.
  • The overlay stops the glitch when the round ends, does not show a finished round again after a reload of OBS or a save of the settings, drops a round left over from before a restart of Streamer.bot, picks up a new fade time and figure on save, and keeps long hints and lists inside the source at a scale above 100 %.
  • An automatic round that could not start no longer uses up the chat lines the next one waits for, and a time-up found by the timer goes to the platform of its round.
  • Free mode switched from your own action answers on that action's platform, not the last one the game saw.
  • The window's note on the stats names the variables the game writes (hm_gamesPlayed, hm_lettersFound).
  • A download GitHub does not deliver, or one that breaks off, is tried three times before the settings action gives up.
  • No answer from the game shows as no answer. A Try button said "done" and a table showed as empty when the game action did not answer, or ran without answering.
  • A late answer is not taken for the next one. Every request to the game has a variable of its own.
  • Another game's newer UIFramework no longer locks this window. The update notice and the live check for automatic rounds loaded the newest UIFramework installed, also one that needs a newer settings action than Hangman's, and the settings window then would not open. They take the newest that fits now, and when that one is damaged, the next older one instead of none until Streamer.bot restarts.
  • A save reaches the game also while the game is still answering another request of the window. It never heard of such a save, and the overlay and the timer for automatic rounds went on with the old settings.
  • A chat line that comes in while the window saves plays by your settings, not by the defaults. A configs.json.bak left without its configs.json is read by the window too, as the game reads it, and no longer saved over with the defaults.
  • Automatic rounds switched off stay off also when Random time draws the next wait at the moment you save.
  • An overlay opacity from before v13, such as 0.29, comes over as 29 %, not as 28.999999999999996.
  • The Help page's Fire with sample values no longer freezes the window while the game is busy, and says why the game did not answer.
  • The Log page's folder button opens Chat Games\Logs beside Streamer.bot, also after a file dialog such as the window's Export was used, and lines written in the same second show newest first.

The save is now passed on up to three times, and if it still does not arrive, a note beside the window says so.

The update notice and the live check loaded the newest UIFramework.dll installed, also one a later game had fetched for a newer settings action, and after every start of Streamer.bot the window then failed to open. entry.title: RhymeTime v2.4.2: The update question says when to restart Streamer.bot
entry.content:
Added

  • aaskjer on Twitch is back among the links of the About page.
  • The window in French and Brazilian Portuguese. Beside English, German and Spanish, the window's language (the pencil, then Language) now offers French and Brazilian Portuguese. Buttons, dialogs, pages and the settings these chat games share follow the language you pick; RhymeTime's own settings and messages read in English, or in German.

Changed

  • A line to finish no longer loses a round to ordinary chat. Every message from the player used to count as a failed attempt, so three lines of talk ended the round. A message counts now when its last word ends like the last word of one of your answers, the same two letters a word needs.

  • One listed rhyme gives a longer ending. Half of the word, but never less than three letters: DOVE on its own accepts anything ending in OVE instead of in VE, which used to let HAVE, GIVE and MOVE win.

  • The attempt limit of a running round is the one it started with. Changing it in the settings mid-round takes effect with the next round, so the dots on the overlay and the limit always agree.

  • The update question says when Streamer.bot needs a restart. A newer UIFramework can be used at once only while none is running in your Streamer.bot; otherwise it takes effect after a restart. The dialog now says which of the two it is, and after such a download a note says it again: restart when it suits you, everything goes on as before until then.

  • Closing the update question means "not now". Yes takes the new UIFramework, No skips that version, and Cancel, the X and Esc ask again at the next open. Closing the dialog used to skip the version for good.

  • A skipped version is skipped in every game. It is kept once, in UIFramework\loader.json beside Streamer.bot, and so is "autoUpdate": false. What a game's uiframework.layout.json holds is still read.

  • The settings action is 0.3.2, the host block UIFramework 2.0.0's, and the next open of the window offers UIFramework 2.0.0. Nothing in your settings changes.

Fixed

  • A rhyme with a ! behind it counts. Punctuation and symbols are dropped from a guess, on both sides of every comparison: dream!, (Dream.) and dream :) all answer DREAM. They used to miss the word and not even count as an attempt, so the chatter saw nothing happen at all.
  • A line to finish is compared word by word. Double spaces in what was typed, and an apostrophe or a comma in the answer you wrote into the word bank, used to make the right answer unreachable.
  • A free round needs no points. A chatter whose points variable does not exist yet was turned away with nothing in chat to say why, even when nothing was at stake. A free round no longer asks for a balance at all, and a chatter who has never earned any counts as 0 in a game with stakes.
  • A balance that cannot be read is left alone. Winning, losing, a battle's stake and its refund worked from 0 when Streamer.bot could not hand over the current balance, which wrote that 0 back and wiped what the chatter had. Nothing is written now, and the log says what was not paid.
  • A round pays out to the chatter it belongs to. Every chat line is handled on a thread of its own in one shared instance, so a round that was settling could take its name, its id or its settings from whatever line arrived meanwhile. A round and a battle now carry their player, platform and settings with them.
  • The block list holds in a battle. Somebody who may not play could still type the winning rhyme and be paid the prize.
  • A battle that times out reports the stake going back. battlePreviousPoints, battleNewPoints and the log line showed zeroes for the moderator who got their stake returned.
  • The dictionary check is no longer switched off by TLS. Where something pinned Streamer.bot to an older TLS, the lookup at wordotron.com failed and every guess with the right ending passed unchecked.
  • The word bank is written beside the file and swapped in, the replaced file kept as .bak, so a write cut short cannot leave half a word bank behind.
  • Seconds to answer and how long the result shows keep the window's limits when the file was edited by hand; a hand-written number used to be able to stop a round from starting at all.
  • The overlay stops waiting for an answer that never comes (five seconds), so a dropped reply no longer leaves it without the round it should pick up after a reload.
  • A message whose platform cannot be told is not played. It used to leave a round nothing could answer and a state under a name no overlay asks for.
  • A download GitHub does not deliver is tried three times before the settings action gives up, also one that breaks off halfway.
  • No answer from the game shows as no answer. A Try button said "done" and a table showed as empty when the game action did not answer.
  • A late answer is not taken for the next one. Every request to the game has a variable of its own.
  • Saving leaves no moment without settings. A round that started while the window swapped the new RT-settings.json in was played on the defaults; the game now waits for the file. With only RT-settings.json.bak left, the window reads it as the game does, where it showed the defaults and its first save wrote them over your settings.
  • Reset all keeps the word bank rows you have not saved yet. The word banks are not reset, as the question says, but rows typed and not saved were thrown away without a word.
  • The questions after the check before saving stay with the window. When you went to another window while the game checked, Check your settings belonged to none: the settings window could be closed under it and not opened again until it was answered.
  • The Log page's folder button opens Chat Games\Logs beside Streamer.bot, also after the window's Export or Import, which used to make it create an empty folder elsewhere. Rounds settled in the same second show newest first.
  • The update notice names only a UIFramework the window would offer. A version skipped with No, or any while "autoUpdate": false, was named in chat at every start.

entry.title: Blackjack Game v17.5.4: Points that stay where they belong
entry.content:
Added

  • The settings window in French and Brazilian Portuguese. Its language picker offers English, German, Spanish, French and Brazilian Portuguese. The window's own texts and the settings every chat game shares come in all five, the game's own settings in English and German.

Changed

  • The settings action is 0.3.2, the host block UIFramework 2.0.0's. The window offers UIFramework 2.0.0 on its next open. Nothing in your settings changes.

Fixed

Points that were lost or made up:

  • quit and the timeout after a split hand back only what is still open. Both used to return every hand's stake, the ones already settled included: a busted first hand came back in full, a won one was paid twice.
  • The payout cut takes from the winnings only. It took its share of the whole return, stake included, so at 50% a win only gave the stake back and above that a win was a loss. The House table did the same; duels were right.
  • Switching Free Game mid-hand no longer moves points. A hand, a duel and a challenge keep the mode they started in: a duel played for points pays out after !SetFreeBlackjack, a challenge's stake comes back after it, and a free hand quit after !EndFreeBlackjack returns nothing it never took. Closing Streamer.bot hands back what was taken the same way.
  • Closing Streamer.bot while a House table takes seats returns the seats' bets. They used to be lost.
  • !SetFreeBlackjack leaves a settings file it cannot read alone. It used to write the switch alone over it, resetting every other setting and pushing the last good save out of the .bak. It now says so in the log, and saving once in the window repairs the file.
  • A payout landing while !blackjack deals is kept. The balance is read again just before the stake is taken.
  • quit is for everyone. The import gave the command to moderators only.
  • Duel raises check the raiser too. Points spent elsewhere after asking to double or split could be staked without being there; the same goes for sudden death.
  • A hand that cannot be dealt returns its stake.

The rules:

  • Without a peek the dealer's blackjack counts. A natural against an Ace or a ten waits for the dealer's second card and pushes on a dealer blackjack; a 21 from more cards loses to one instead of going to a tie-break. In House Mode the European table does the same.
  • Insurance is always settled. Without a peek a hand that ended in a bust or a 5-card Charlie kept the insurance stake without a word; it is now paid or lost on the dealer's second card. Once the dealer has peeked it is no longer offered.
  • Split hands that tie are settled last. A tie-break's extra dealer cards changed what the other hands were compared with.
  • A split A+10 in a duel is 21, not blackjack.
  • Surrender keeps the odd point for the house: a bet of 1 no longer surrenders for free.
  • 1,5k is 1,500 and 0,5k is 500 (the comma read as a thousands separator: 15,000). 1,500 stays 1,500.
  • Free Game lets a viewer without points play, !blackjack all included.
  • Accepting a duel checks the House table and your own challenge, and a challenged player cannot take a seat meanwhile. A second duel used to overwrite the first, which then could not be played. Accepting your own challenge is refused too.
  • The games-per-hour limit follows Duels count toward Games per hour for both players.

Stats and triggers:

  • A push counts its stake as returned. netProfit dropped by the stake on every push.
  • A split round counts once in gamesPlayed, and !stats gives the win rate over hands: it could pass 100%.
  • Free Game records no amounts, losses included; a free duel moves no duel points.
  • A House surrender counts as a lost hand, and House insurance and quit fire BJG: Hand Settled and BJG: House Hand Settled like everything else.
  • bjg_userName is no longer overwritten with the name of whoever settled the table.
  • The weekly reset follows ISO weeks: around New Year it fired up to three times in eight days.

The rest:

  • The cooldown replies cannot break: a {user} or a brace in them made them fail silently. {user} now works there too.
  • The overlay clears a finished hand. The next hand's cards deal in again, a refreshed source no longer replays an old result, and a House table picking its rules waits behind a running hand instead of an empty table.
  • The demo explains how to place it in OBS: untick Local file and use the overlay's file:/// address with ?demo=1; &demo=1 did nothing.
  • Create the browser source in OBS and Reset the leaderboard now use the values in the window, saved or not, and the OBS setup writes the overlay into the folder it points the source at.
  • The shoe keeps its size after a rare emergency reshuffle; settings that could not be read are logged; the shared tables are read under the lock.
  • The Resplit help no longer says split Aces can be split again.

The settings window:

  • The cooldown replies' Bot account and Send as /me have their switches, on the Messages page. The window showed none for them.
  • A hand dealt while you save reads the saved settings. For the moment the window swapped the new file in, the game read the defaults.
  • Fire with sample values on the Help page no longer freezes the window while the game answers something else.
  • The Log page's folder button opens Chat Games\Logs beside Streamer.bot, and lines written in the same second show newest first.
  • A UIFramework installed for a newer game no longer locks this window. The update notice at Streamer.bot's start loads only a UIFramework this settings action fits and passes over a damaged one, and the settings action leaves a running one alone that needs a newer settings action. A download that breaks off midway is tried again too.

Download v17.5.4 · Blackjack Game on aaskjer.github.io

entry.title: UIFramework v2.0.0: UIFramework v2.0.0
entry.content:
The window comes in French and Brazilian Portuguese, a path field opens Windows' file dialog, and a group field suggests Streamer.bot's groups. 2.0.0 starts the v2 line: its latest.json is lib/v2/latest.json, which settings action 0.3.2 reads. A project gets 2.0.0 offered once it ships stub 0.3.2 and its host block; one on an older stub reads lib/v1/latest.json, stays on 1.9.0 and uses 2.0.0 only when another project has installed it. Nothing was removed: the window still works with every settings action from stub 0.1.0 on (MinHostStub stays 0.1.0).

Added

  • French and Brazilian Portuguese. fr.json and pt-BR.json carry every page, key, placeholder, text and window text, translated from the revised English and read a second time; no native speaker has read them yet. The language picker takes the width of its longest name now, at least the 110 px it had and at most 220, so "Português (Brasil)" is no longer cut off. A test holds every language file the DLL carries to English's entries and placeholders.
  • "Fix a translation", an issue form for the window's texts in any language. It asks for the language, what the window says now and what it should say. It links the new section Proofreading a language in docs/Conventions.md, which shows how to try a wording first in a UIFramework\lang\<code>.json beside Streamer.bot.
  • A path field has a button for Windows' file or folder dialog. docs/Schema.md promised "a folder/file dialog", but the field was a text box with a button that only opened the folder in Explorer. The new button opens a file dialog when the value or the default names a file (it has an extension, or a file of that name exists), otherwise a folder dialog. The dialog starts where the value points, or where the default points while the value is empty; a relative value counts from the Streamer.bot folder. A file the action has not written yet can be chosen. A choice is written as a full path, also under the Streamer.bot folder: a project may read a relative value from a folder of its own.
  • A grouplist field suggests Streamer.bot's groups (stub 0.3.2). docs/Schema.md promised "chips with Streamer.bot's groups suggested"; the field had the hint "Add a Streamer.bot group" and took what was typed. The first time a group field gets the cursor, the window asks the settings action for the groups, once. The action reads them with CPH.GetGroups() on Streamer.bot's thread, and the window stays usable meanwhile. A list under the box then shows the groups not added yet, narrowed by what is typed: Up and Down pick one, Enter or a click adds it, Esc closes the list. Enter without a picked group adds what was typed, as before. The list comes with the DLL, the groups with stub 0.3.2; with an older settings action, and in the preview, the field works as it did.
  • A request that takes long on purpose says it is still at work: UiHost.StillWorking() (host block, stub 0.3.2). The project calls it while such a request runs (a Try button that imports a word list), and the settings action waits 30 seconds from then for the answer. It gave every request 30 seconds from its start and then dropped the answer while the work went on; Hangman stopped its import at 28 seconds for that. Without the call, a request still gets 30 seconds. A request from a window opened again meanwhile waits for one that says it still works instead of starting beside it after 35 seconds, and a request that hung before it no longer takes its StillWorking() away when it ends. See The game's side in docs/Schema.md.

Changed

  • The update dialog says when Streamer.bot needs a restart (stub 0.3.1). A newer UIFramework can be used at once only while none runs in this Streamer.bot; a project that loads it at the start (the update notice, UiLive) or a window opened before keeps the running one in use. The dialog now says which case it is: "Streamer.bot needs no restart", or "takes effect once Streamer.bot is restarted" with the version that runs until then. After a download that has to wait, a second note says it once more (restart Streamer.bot; no hurry, it can wait until after the stream). Before, the window opened as usual and only the log told. Nothing changes in the DLL; a project gets it when it ships stub 0.3.1 or later.
  • A language code means its language in any case, and across a region. The layout file's language, a project's fixed language (InLanguage), the codes of its Lang and the names of the files in UIFramework\lang were matched letter for letter. "language": "DE" or "de-AT" opened the window in English, and a project's Lang("pt-br", …) beside the DLL's pt-BR, or a pt-br.json beside Streamer.bot, added a second Portuguese to the picker whose words never reached the framework's. Now a code matches a language in any case. A regional code falls back to its language (de-AT is German), a language to its only regional file (pt is pt-BR), and anything else to English. The picker, the layout file and the update notice keep the language file's spelling.
  • An en.json in UIFramework\lang corrects English. A file there was laid over every language the DLL carries except English, which always came from the DLL, so a proofreader's corrections to English never showed. It is now read when the window opens, as de.json there is. Without such a file, English is the DLL's own, loaded once.
  • The window's texts in English, German and Spanish are read again. Stiff wording is plainer now, and a text that meant whatever the window belongs to, rather than a game, says "extension". Three said what the window does not do and are corrected: the accent colour holds for this extension's window only, Reset layout also takes the help under the fields back into the tooltips, and a newer version shows as a red label at the top of the window, not on the About page.
  • The Help page comes by itself when the window declares help sections, custom triggers or methods and does not name help among its pages, as Messages and About already did. The triggers with their Fire buttons and the method list had no page.
  • The red "i" names a log declared without its page, and a range slider whose whole default meets a fraction. A window with Log(folder, files) that does not name log had no Log page and no switch for the log, without a word. A range slider's default decides what it holds (docs/Schema.md), so S("x", 1, kind: "slider", min: 0, max: 2, step: 0.5) is a slider of whole numbers on a 0.5 grid: it saves 0.5 as 0 and 1.5 as 2, the same as the place next to each, and nothing said so. The rule stays; the check names a slider whose default is a whole number while its step, minimum or maximum has a fraction, and says to write the default as 1.0 for a slider of decimals.
  • An action's status reaches the footer also when the action has a panel. With a panel, and so with every auto action, the status went nowhere, or into the panel only while the panel was empty, and the documented answer with lines, bar, set and status could not be shown whole. The footer now shows the status beside the panel.
  • An emote field with platform: youtube shows its picture, as a list's emote column does: YouTube's own emojis (:name:) from the table inside the DLL. The single field had no picture at all.
  • The docs are read again, README and docs/ alike, as the code now is and for any project: plainer wording, "project" or "extension" where any user of the framework is meant, "game" only where a game is. Corrected where text and code disagreed: field help as a tooltip, units in the label, step only for sliders, a percent compared as stored, path and grouplist as they now work, the accent colour per extension, Lock(), the Log page's order, what keeps a 2.x DLL from a 1.x settings action, the troubleshooting rows. README's tree and tool list follow the repository. The demo's README counts the settings it declares as they are and names the tick on Precompile on Application Start that the update notice needs.
  • The demo and the mirrors in hosts/ carry the host block of stub 0.3.2, and the demo's import is built again.
  • CI runs once per commit and checks what is made from the sources. It ran on every push to every branch, and a branch with a pull request had each check run twice; it now runs on pushes to main and on pull requests. Beside the build, the tests and docs/Conventions.md, it checks that the demo and the eight games' copies in hosts/ carry the template's host block and that the demo's import carries the demo and the stub.
  • The release workflow runs CI's checks as well. It does not wait for CI, and 1.6.0 was published while CI failed on its docs/Conventions.md. A tag is released only when the conventions doc, the demo's host block and the demo's import pass there too.
  • Leftovers are gone. The seven facades in hosts/ (six games' SettingsFacade.cs and Blackjack's StatsFacade.cs) were copies of the games' settings classes from the port to the generic stub; nothing read them, and they had drifted from the games. Three empty .gitkeep files are gone with them, and tools/spec-to-window.ps1 leaves too: no project has had a spec.json of its own since 1.9.0.

Fixed

In the DLL, for every project with the next UIFramework release:

  • A save keeps what changed while the project checked it. A save waits for the project's validate. An answer that came in meanwhile (a preset button's or an ask field's set) or a timer put its values into the fields after the save had taken its copy, and the window said "Saved" with no unsaved change while the file held the old values: closing asked nothing, and the values were gone. They now count as unsaved, the status line says how many, Save & Exit asks before it closes, and the next save writes them.
  • The questions after the project's check belong to the window. When the project took its time and the user went to another window meanwhile, Not checked and Check your settings (and the notes after a save or an import that failed) had no owner. The settings window took clicks again with the save still open, its X closed it while the question stayed up, and the settings could not be opened again until that question was answered. The questions are now modal to the settings window.
  • Reset all keeps the unsaved rows of a list in a file of its own. Such a list is not reset, as the question says, but rows typed into it and not yet saved were replaced by the file's without a word, and the status said "No unsaved changes". They stay in the list now, still unsaved, as Reset page leaves them.
  • The red "i" speaks of an unreadable list file in the window's language. The line was English in every window. It now names the list and its file, followed by the list's own tooltip (list.unreadable).
  • A settings file gone beside its .bak is shown from the .bak, as the project reads it. When the settings file was missing and its .bak lay beside it (a swap that was cut off, or a file deleted by hand), the project's UiSettings.Load ran on the .bak, but the window showed the defaults, and its first save, an import or Reset all wrote them over what the project was using. The window now reads the .bak too and says so in the log and in a line under the red "i"; its next save writes the settings file from the values it shows. A file that was never saved still gives the defaults on both sides.
  • A null in the settings file stands for the setting's default, in the window as in the project. The host block's UiSettings reads past a null to an old key, then to the default. The window took the null as the value and showed 0, an empty box or a switch that is off, none of which the project went by, and dropped an old key's value beside it. It now reads the default (or the old key's value) as the host block does, and the next save writes that in place of the null. An import that names a setting with null brings nothing for it.
  • An old key's factor leaves no float noise in the settings file. An old fraction moved to a percent with its factor of 100, such as 0.29, was written as 28.999999999999996 while the box showed 29 (Hangman's overlay opacity, whose default is a decimal). The moved value is now rounded to ten decimals, as a number box saves it. The host block rounds it the same way (below).
  • An import takes a slider's value through the slider. It wrote whatever the file named for a slider: a number beyond its range, text where its number belongs, a stop it does not have. The window then showed the slider at its end and called the value corrected, while the project read the file's value until the next save. A number is now pulled into the range (to a whole number on a whole-number slider); text or a stop the slider lacks is not taken, and the dialog says why, as for a dropdown. If the import names the value the slider already holds, one none of its stops offers, that value stays.
  • An import trims a token, a path, a colour and an emote as a save does. A token with a line break after it in the imported file was written with it and stayed so until the field was changed. A plain text field still keeps the spaces at either end, as typed.
  • A click on the stop a slider sits on chooses it. A slider over stops that holds a value none of them offers names that value beside its label and sits on its first stop. A click on that stop's caption or on the thumb chose the stop without the window noticing: the count of unsaved changes stayed the same, a condition on the slider did not follow, and a field with ask did not ask the project. It now counts as one change.
  • A slider over decimal stops finds the stop of its number. A default or a set of 2.0 arrives as 2, and with the stops "0.5", "2.0" and "5.0" it was taken for the index of the third stop: the slider showed Fast and the next save wrote "5.0". A number now finds the stop of the same value however either is written ("0.50" is the stop "0.5"); an index finds a stop only among stops that are no numbers.
  • A slider over a range starts on its default when the file holds no number. With "" or "abc" stored, it sat on its minimum, and the next save wrote that minimum. It now does what a number box does: it shows the default, and the save writes it.
  • A field with ask asks with the values the window shows. It sent the saved ones. A preset slider that moved from live to ask (the name 1.9.0 gave it) was answered for the stop it was saved on, and set put that stop's numbers back. On such a field ask now means what live meant, as docs/Schema.md says. A window of 1.9.0 does it with live beside ask, which the host block of stub 0.3.2 writes by itself (below).
  • An ask field's answers land in the order it asked. An answer that waited behind another request of the settings action and came after a later one put its values over the later one's: the slider stood on one stop and the fields held another stop's numbers. The field numbers its questions as a button does, and a late answer to an earlier one is dropped.
  • An action's box no longer says it failed after an answer came. When a Try button's ask failed (the project did not answer in time) and the next answer only set fields or brought a status, the box went on showing the failure. That answer takes the failure's place now: its status shows, or the box hides when there is none. The lines of an earlier answer still stay under one that only sets fields.
  • An answer under a row hides with its action also with the help under the fields. With help lines on, a button in a named row whose condition hid it left its answer box showing under the row.
  • The Help page's Fire button no longer freezes the window, and it says why the action did not answer. It asked the project's action on the window's own thread: with another request still running, the window froze for five seconds, and the settings action's reason for no answer was replaced by the hint that the action may run an older version. It now asks the way a Try button has since 1.9.0. The button stays greyed until the answer comes, and no answer shows the settings action's reason. An answer that is none at all (a host block that does not know the request) keeps the older-version hint.
  • The project's emote sources are asked without holding the window still. The window asked for them (the broadcaster's Twitch id and token, the project's own YouTube pictures) on its own thread. As the first emote field was built, that froze the window for up to five seconds while the action was busy; a Try box with YouTube emotes (:name:), asking before any emote field had, waited up to 35 seconds when the project's handler hung. They are now asked once per window on another thread, and each picture shows once the answer has come. A shortcode holds its picture's place until then and is drawn as text when it has none. A Unicode emoji still shows at once.
  • The tooltip of a 7TV, BTTV or FFZ emote picture is in the window's language. It was built in English in code; it is now the window text field.emote.extension, in every language the DLL carries.
  • A sender switch the Messages page does not draw is a field on its page. The window kept useBot, sendAction, numberSeparator and the two cooldown switches for the Messages page, which draws them only while it has messages, and the cooldown pair only while a message is in the cooldown group. A project without messages, or one whose cooldown messages have no group (Blackjack's), had settings its action reads and no field for them. Such a switch is now a field on its own page (general, cooldowns, or the page it declares), and a page that names one shows it. A standard page with nothing of its own (Messages without messages, Help without help) now shows the fields declared for it; before, it was left out together with them.
  • hidden hides the sender switches, the number format and the log switch. The Messages and Log pages drew them hidden or not; only Senders(useBot: null) left one out. A setting the project hides (hidden, Override(key, hidden: true)) has no field there now, and its value stays in the file.
  • A page's own title stays in a language that does not title its id. In a language with only the project's own texts (Lang("nl", …)) or a language file without page titles, the conventions' English title replaced the declared one: "How to play" read "Help", "Scoreboard" read "Leaderboard". As with a key's label, the conventions' title for the id is taken only where it is a translation.
  • The red "i" looks for split sections on the page a field ends up on. It read the page each setting declared, before the window's pages claimed their fields. So it called a section split that a page's claim had put back together, and missed one that a page collecting the fields of two pages split.
  • The timer's random switch sits on the row of its two intervals, and the longest wait greys out with the timer's switch too, as docs/Schema.md says. The random switch stood on a line of its own, and with it on, the longest wait stayed open while the timer was off.
  • The About page translates the credits and the project's own links. The Tx translations of the credits under the name and of the texts in About(links:) were not used, although the page's sections and the links inside them were translated and docs/Schema.md said Tx translates the credits. They now go through the same lookup as every other declared text.
  • Customise mode: Move up and Move down move a field on the page it is shown on. The sender switches, the number format and the log switch, which the Messages and Log pages draw wherever they are declared, counted among a page's fields. On High-Low's Cooldowns page and Blackjack's Messages page a press went past one of them and nothing moved, the first field shown could still be moved up, and a field moved next to one took a section the page does not show. They are left out now.
  • Customise mode: Move up and Move down cross a heading one place at a time. The first field under a heading, moved up, landed between the last two fields of the section above; the last field of a section, moved down, went past the first field of the next. The places next to a heading could only be reached with the mouse. A step over a heading now takes the field into that section and leaves it where it stands.
  • Customise mode: a field moved to another page no longer splits a section there. Move to page and a drop on a page in the rail left the field at its declared place among all settings, which on a page the user had sorted fell anywhere, often between two fields of one section, whose heading then showed twice. The field now goes to the end of its own section when that page has it, else to the end of the page, on a line of its own. The menu takes it out of its row too, as the drop did.
  • Customise mode: on a page the user sorted, a field the user never placed goes where the project declares it. Sorting a page gives each of its fields an order in the layout file. A field without one, which the project added in an update or Reset this field gave back, kept its place among all the project's settings; on a sorted page that place could be anywhere, often inside another section, whose heading then showed twice. It now goes behind the field the project declares before it on that page when the two share a section, else to the end of its own section there, else to the end of the page.
  • An order typed into the layout file with too many digits no longer keeps the window from opening. A whole number longer than 19 digits made every open fail. It now reads as the largest order, as a value of the wrong kind reads as not set.
  • The folder button of a path field opens the folder a file is in. For a value that names a file (overlay\state.json), the button made a folder with the file's name, after which the action could not write its file there; for a file that already existed it failed, and only the log said so. It now opens the file's folder, and creates that folder when it is missing, as it does for a folder.
  • Log page: the folder button opens the log folder beside Streamer.bot. It opened the declared folder (Chat Games/Logs) relative to the process's current directory, which a file dialog moves (the window's own Export and Import, any dialog of Streamer.bot). After an export to the Desktop it created and opened an empty Desktop\Chat Games\Logs. It now opens the folder the page follows and the settings action reads, under the Streamer.bot folder.
  • Log page: lines written in the same second show newest first. The page sorts by time, which has whole seconds, and kept lines of equal time in the order it got them. The settings action hands them over as they were written, so lines written together, several in one second, showed oldest first inside a list that is newest first. The last line written is now the first row, on open and on every reload.
  • Log page: a line without a readable time leaves the Time column empty. It showed 0001-01-01 00:00:00. A click on the column header still sorts by time.
  • The update notice leaves out a UIFramework release the settings would not offer. A release skipped with No in the update dialog, or any release while the release check is off (skipVersion, "autoUpdate": false in UIFramework\loader.json), was named in chat at every Streamer.bot start, and the log line sent the streamer to settings that did not offer it. The notice now follows the settings action's rules. A project whose own uiframework.layout.json skips the release or switches the check off counts as not offering it, and UIFramework is named while at least one project of the run would offer it. An unreadable loader.json counts as empty, as in the settings action. The projects' own releases are named as before.
  • A language file with broken braces no longer costs the update notice. A file in UIFramework\lang beside Streamer.bot whose import it again text had lost a brace made the notice throw while it was put together, and that Streamer.bot run had no notice. The text is now filled the way the window fills its own, and a text with broken braces is used as it stands.
  • The update notice uses the language a project fixes for its window. It followed the language in the layout file, which a window with InLanguage("de") never writes, so that project's notice came in English or in a language picked before. The window now tells the notice its fixed language when it opens, and the notice keeps it for the Streamer.bot starts that follow.
  • The chat preview groups amounts as the window's language does, for a project without a thousands-separator setting. It wrote 1,500 in English and 1.500 in every other language. Now it takes the separator Windows gives the language: 1.500 in German, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese, 1 500 in French. French officially uses a narrow no-break space; the preview writes a plain space, which chat and the text box both show. A language Windows does not know keeps the point.

In the settings action, for a project that ships stub 0.3.2:

  • A running UIFramework that needs a newer settings action is not taken (stub 0.3.2). A host block of 1.9.0 or before, in another project, still loads the newest DLL as Streamer.bot starts. The stub passed such a DLL over when it was installed but used it when it was running, and the DLL then refused the window with the advice to remove its folder. The stub now leaves it alone in both cases; its dialog names the running version and the stub it needs, and says that updating the project opens the window.
  • A damaged DLL is set aside also while an older UIFramework runs (stub 0.3.2). As Streamer.bot starts, the host block passes over a newest UIFramework.dll that fails its hash and loads the next older one. The settings action then used the running one without checking the newest, so the damaged file stayed where it was: its version was never offered again, and at every start the log said it would be used from the next one. The settings action now checks the hash of the DLL it chose also beside a running UIFramework and sets a damaged file aside as .broken; the next open offers that version again.
  • The release check's log line calls the installed version installed (stub 0.3.2). With a project that loads UIFramework as Streamer.bot starts, the line called the newest installed version "in use" while an older one ran, and when the chosen DLL had failed and been set aside, the log still said it would be used from the next start. The line now says "installed". The next-start line comes only when the chosen DLL is still there beside a UIFramework that ran before the window opened.
  • The project hears of every save (stub 0.3.2). The "saved" request runs from the settings action's queue. When it found another request still running, the log said "A queued step failed" and the project never heard of the save, so its overlay and timed action went on with the old settings. It is now sent again, three tries in all, and what still fails is said in the log and in a note beside the window. A run of the project's action that ended without answering counts as not heard too.
  • A download that breaks off is tried again (stub 0.3.2). A connection reset while the file came in was not counted as a broken connection, and a connection closed early left a short file that failed the hash check with a message that read like tampering. Both get the three tries now, as does a connection that cannot be made; only after the last one does the dialog say that the file does not match.
  • A project's action that runs without answering is "no answer" (stub 0.3.2). One whose Execute() never reached UiHost.Handle counted as an empty answer: a Try button said "done", and a save went on as checked. Streamer.bot reads a global set to empty text back as null, so the stub now marks the answer's variable before the run and sees whether the project wrote it.
  • A DLL in a folder named 1.9 gets the no-answer marker (stub 0.3.2). It was compared as older than 1.9.0 and got null instead.
  • A list or an object where a version belongs no longer breaks every open (stub 0.3.2). skipVersion in loader.json or the layout file, or minHostStub in latest.json, made the window fail. Such a value counts as missing now, and the log says so.
  • An unreadable loader.json is not written over (stub 0.3.2). A damaged or locked UIFramework\loader.json counted as empty, and No in the update dialog replaced it with a file holding only skipVersion. It now counts as empty without being written over, as the layout file already did; No keeps the skip in the project's layout file then, and the log says where it went (or that it could not be kept) and that loader.json cannot be read.
  • A run that a later one took over ends there (stub 0.3.2). When a project's action that had hung for a minute answered after all, its first run went on to the update dialog and the window, beside the run that had opened it.
  • Two runs that end together leave the window free (stub 0.3.2). If the run that opened the window ended just as another run's window closed, neither handed the window back, and the next open reused the old schema without asking the project or GitHub.

In the host block, for a project that ships the host block of stub 0.3.2:

  • A DLL that needs a newer settings action no longer locks a project's window (host block). The update notice and UiLive loaded the newest UIFramework.dll under lib\, also one another project had installed for a newer stub. Only one UIFramework runs in a Streamer.bot, so the project's settings window then failed on every start, although the stub passes such a DLL over. The host block now loads the newest DLL that fits the settings action released with it (StubVersion in the host block, 0.3.2, kept equal to the stub's); a DLL that names no stub fits. The block reads the DLL's version without System.dll, so it still compiles in an action that lists only mscorlib, System.Core, Newtonsoft.Json and Streamer.bot's interface.
  • The update notice takes the next older DLL when the newest cannot be used (host block). When the newest UIFramework.dll under lib\ failed its hash or threw once while loading, the block gave up on every DLL for the rest of the run: no update notice, and UiLive said Unknown for Twitch and Kick until Streamer.bot restarted. It now tries the installed ones newest first and passes over one that is damaged, will not load, or needs a newer settings action (the entry above); a file downloaded again is tried again. Once a UIFramework is loaded, the block takes that one: .NET answers every later load of a UIFramework.dll, whichever version, with the one already loaded.
  • UiSettings.Load during a save reads the saved settings (host block). The window swaps the new settings file in, the old one becoming the .bak, and for that moment there is no file. UiSettings.Load took the missing file for one never saved and gave the defaults without a word. It now waits a moment for a file that is being swapped in, and reads the .bak (saying so in Problem) when only that is left. A file missing beside its .bak with no save under way is read from the .bak at once, without the wait; a project whose settings were never saved still gets the defaults at once.
  • A save that switches the timer off keeps it off (host block). UiTimer.Rearm looked at the timed action, then switched it off and on; a save whose UiTimer.Sync switched it off in between found it on again. The two now take turns.
  • UiSettings reads an old key that is a setting of its own for that setting only (host block). A setting whose aliases named another setting's key read that setting's value while its own key was not in the file yet. The window leaves such an old key alone (the red "i" names it) and showed the default, so the project ran on another setting's value until the first save. It now gets the default, as the window shows.
  • An old value moved with aliasFactor is read as the window stores it (host block). UiSettings multiplied it as it was, so an old fraction of 0.07 became 7.000000000000001 percent in the project, also in a message that prints it. It is now rounded to ten decimals, as the window's store does.
  • A field with ask is asked with what the window shows, also in a window of 1.9.0 (host block). The released DLL hands a request the window's current values only for a setting marked live, so a field declared with ask alone (a preset slider) was answered from the values saved last, not from where the slider stood. The host block now writes live beside ask for every field that is no button.

In this repository's tools and workflows:

  • The release workflow refuses an empty changelog section also when the next heading follows at once. PowerShell counts a range down as well: with no line between the version's heading and the next one, both headings were taken as the notes, and an empty section was released.
  • tools/check-stub.ps1 compiles into a folder of its own per checkout. Two checkouts (worktrees) checked at once compiled into the same Stub.dll and Demo.dll, so one failed on a file the other had open, or read the other's demo for its schema.json.
  • tools/update-host-block.ps1 knows the earlier templates of every branch. It read the lines of earlier host blocks from the checked-out history only. A project can carry the block of a branch not merged yet, and a plain git log also leaves out a merged branch whose merge kept the other side's file; such lines counted as the project's own.
  • tools/docs-shots.ps1 takes Newtonsoft.Json from the preview's build. It loaded it from a Streamer.bot folder that was its default on one machine only, and elsewhere the run stopped after seven of its eight windows. -StreamerBotPath is gone; no Streamer.bot folder is needed.

entry.title: High-Low Game v2.3.2: Outcome words, renamed commands, and when to restart Streamer.bot
entry.content:
Added

  • The outcome message speaks your language, all of it. What {result}, {emoji}, {sign} and {pointsSection} say (correct, incorrect, won, lost, ...) was fixed English; it is now on the Messages page under Outcome words.
  • Renamed commands still play. The game and the scoreboard know their commands by their ID, so a command renamed in Streamer.bot or given an alias works as before.

Changed

  • A tie on the scoreboard goes to fewer guesses. With as many wins, the player who needed fewer guesses is ahead, and the same wins in the same number of guesses share a place. It used to go by name.

  • The broadcaster or bot, left out of the scoreboard, gets their own stats when they ask for it, instead of being told they are "sadly not in the Top 5".

  • Session stats are kept by user ID, like the all-time ones: two YouTube viewers with the same display name no longer share one.

  • The update question says when Streamer.bot needs a restart. A newer UIFramework can be used at once only while none is running in your Streamer.bot; otherwise it takes effect after a restart. The dialog now says which of the two it is, and after such a download a note says it again: restart when it suits you, everything goes on as before until then.

  • Closing the update question means "not now". Yes takes the new UIFramework, No skips that version, and Cancel, the X and Esc ask again at the next open. Closing the dialog used to skip the version for good.

  • A skipped version is skipped in every game. It is kept once, in UIFramework\loader.json beside Streamer.bot, and so is "autoUpdate": false. What a game's uiframework.layout.json holds is still read.

  • The settings action is 0.3.1, the host block UIFramework 1.9.0's. Nothing in your settings changes.

Fixed

  • A download GitHub does not deliver is tried three times before the settings action gives up.
  • No answer from the game shows as no answer. A Try button said "done" and a table showed as empty when the game action did not answer.
  • A late answer is not taken for the next one. Every request to the game has a variable of its own.
  • Messages fit YouTube. YouTube takes 200 characters per message; the scoreboards, !hlgpersonal and a long outcome went out in one piece of up to 490 and were cut off. Every message is now sent in pieces that fit the platform (200 on YouTube, 500 on Twitch and Kick), cut between words.
  • A blocked viewer gets no reply at all. A blocked viewer on cooldown got the cooldown message, and so did a Twitch chat command while guesses come from channel points.
  • A typed bet of 1.5 is refused, not read as 15 (or 2,50 as 250). Thousands separators still work: 1.500 is 1500.
  • A game reward redeemed while channel points are off is refunded. It used to keep the channel points and play nothing.
  • Two guesses at the same moment both count. The draw, the counters and the points change now happen one guess at a time; two at once could read the same balance and lose one of the two changes.
  • The log and hlg_last* no longer show the last player's points for a guess whose balance could not be read.
  • A bot account that cannot be read no longer puts the broadcaster on the scoreboard.
  • !hlgpersonal without a user (a test trigger) logs a warning instead of looking up the stats of nobody.
  • How to play names guessSessionGuesses and guessAlltimeGuesses among the trigger arguments, and says that the number is kept across restarts (it is not drawn anew at every start).

entry.title: Trivia Game v9.3.2: The update question says when to restart Streamer.bot
entry.content:
Changed

  • The update question says when Streamer.bot needs a restart. A newer UIFramework can be used at once only while none is running in your Streamer.bot; otherwise it takes effect after a restart. The dialog now says which of the two it is, and after such a download a note says it again: restart when it suits you, everything goes on as before until then.
  • Closing the update question means "not now". Yes takes the new UIFramework, No skips that version, and Cancel, the X and Esc ask again at the next open. Closing the dialog used to skip the version for good.
  • A skipped version is skipped in every game. It is kept once, in UIFramework\loader.json beside Streamer.bot, and so is "autoUpdate": false. What a game's uiframework.layout.json holds is still read.
  • The settings action is 0.3.1, the host block UIFramework 1.9.0's. Nothing in your settings changes.
  • The monthly reset never takes wins from the new month. It used to run only at the first scoreboard command, and wiped every win since the reset day along with last month's. Now the game applies it too, just before it writes a win, so the reset lands at the first win or scoreboard command on or after the day. Switching a reset off and on again arms it afresh instead of wiping the board mid-month.
  • Tied viewers share their place on the leaderboard (1, 2, 2, 4) and their medal, instead of being ranked in no particular order.
  • The Relaxed difficulty lets two characters differ, not three. Three on words of three letters let any three-letter word through ('lol' counted as 'Red'), which the window's own check warned about.
  • First reminder at 0 sends no reminders. It used to fall back to half the round.
  • A topic of a generated source plays only that source. With your questions mixed in, !trivia pokemon was sometimes answered with one of yours from any category. The categories of your own questions, which chat is offered beside the topics, can now be picked too.
  • Saving the settings restarts the automatic-round timer only when its schedule changed. A save of a message pushed the next automatic round a whole interval further out.
  • Set it up in OBS leaves a source of another kind alone. An image or text source with the overlay's name used to be "pointed at the overlay", which did nothing; the window now says so. A browser source of that name is checked after it is repointed.
  • The Addicted usage message names !TA. It said !addicted, a command the import does not have. A message you saved yourself keeps its text.

Fixed

  • A download GitHub does not deliver is tried three times before the settings action gives up.
  • No answer from the game shows as no answer. A Try button said "done" and a table showed as empty when the game action did not answer.
  • A late answer is not taken for the next one. Every request to the game has a variable of its own.
  • !trivia starts rounds on YouTube and Kick again while channel points start them on Twitch. With Channel points start a round on, every start without a reward was ignored, whatever the platform, although redemptions only exist on Twitch. The round count and the category typed after it work there too.
  • A skip, a force end or a winning blitz answer while the question goes out no longer ends in "Failed to fetch a trivia question" and a cancelled series for a round that was running.
  • !trivia custom plays your questions that have no category. They were offered to chat as Custom but never matched it.
  • Chat noise is no answer. A lone "?", ":)" or an emoji counted as any option made of symbols and locked the viewer out of the round. Text that fits two options alike ('C#.' for C, C# and C++) counts as neither.
  • A number in an answer is right or wrong, never close. 'PlayStation 3' counted as 'PlayStation 4' when the 3 was not offered, and 'Generation V' as 'Generation IV'.
  • Generated questions no longer give their answer away. PokeAPI asked which Pokémon evolves into Pidgeot (Pidgeotto), what type Steelix is (Steel), which is the Ninja Pokémon (Ninjask); IGDB which studio made Sonic Adventure (Sonic Team) and on which platform Mario Kart Wii came out (Wii). Nor does an evolution question offer the stage before last as a wrong answer.
  • IGDB's "which came out first" question is rated by the difficulty it was drawn for, not always medium, so it pays like the others. An answer from IGDB that is no game list keeps the stored list instead of costing the round its question.
  • A source that does not answer is left alone for a while. After a failure, PokeAPI is not asked for ten minutes, IGDB for half an hour and the OdeNet download for a quarter of an hour; every round used to wait out the full timeout again. A stalled OdeNet download is now cut off at its limit instead of holding up every generated source.
  • PokeAPI keeps what it learnt. Types fetched for a stored Pokémon and a refreshed species count are saved too.
  • One payout that fails no longer stops the round. The other winners are paid, and chat, the overlay and the triggers get the result.
  • A very large payout no longer wipes the winner's points. It is capped instead of overflowing to a negative number, which set the balance to 0.
  • Text is decoded once. A question about &nbsp; showed as a blank; your own questions copied out of opentdb, with their " and &, show as text on the overlay too.
  • Two YouTube viewers with the same name answer separately. Answers are told apart by the viewer's id, not the display name. The Addicted list takes a viewer's id as well as their name.
  • A long message is never cut inside an emoji.
  • A blocked viewer who redeems a trivia reward gets the points back, as for any redemption that starts nothing.
  • !trivia ３ is no request for a few billion rounds, and a 0 typed into the multi-round reward plays one round, not the most.
  • A round with an answer time of 0 ends by itself. It stayed open until someone wrote in chat.
  • An automatic turn that finds a round under way keeps the chat lines counted for the next one, and the announcement of a random-time round says when the next one really comes.
  • Two !TA at once both land, and one that cannot be saved changes nothing. The list is changed in configs.json under its lock. A configs.json that does not parse is no longer replaced by a file holding the Addicted list alone.
  • Saving configs.json is tried again when a chat line happens to be reading it at that moment.
  • Rounds of an ad break are planned with the time the overlay's result takes, so they no longer run on well past the ads.
  • An own question whose wrong answers only repeat the right one is not played as a one-option round.
  • The opentdb check says when opentdb only asked to slow down, instead of reporting it down.
  • The log's file names and times are the same on every PC, whatever calendar Windows uses.
  • Scoreboard: a bot or broadcaster that connects after the first command is left off the board; the command that triggers the monthly reset shows the new board, not last month's; the blocked list and !TSS find viewers by login as well as display name; the reset month is the same under every calendar.
  • Overlay: another platform's result no longer replaces a round that is still running; after a reload a running round wins over a finished one; after a lost connection the overlay picks up what happened meanwhile; a wrong password no longer makes it sign in again every second.
  • Help texts and guides name the pages, labels and commands as they are now.
